correctness.rationale: For every real ell_p(Gamma;ell_q²) with infinite Gamma, 1≤p<∞,2≤q≤∞, define s as inf over unit base x of sup over unit y of min two symmetric chord lengths. An unused or arbitrarily small outer coordinate gives the 2^(1/p) lower bound for each x. For finite q≥2, the rotated fiber (r,s)↦(s,−r), scaled coordinatewise by ||x_gamma||_q, is again a unit witness; scalar Clarkson gives both q-power chord norms ≥2, hence both global chords ≥2^(1/q). At one-coordinate base x=(1,0), choose the sign cancelling y first component; with a=||y_fiber||, min chord^p ≤(1+a^q)^(p/q)+1−a^p. For p≤q subadditivity bounds by 2; for p≥q monotonicity in b=a^q bounds by 2^(p/q). For q=∞ the chosen first-fiber chord ≤1 and total ≤2. Thus upper equals max two lower mechanisms, s=2^(1/min(p,q)), including p=q and q=∞ endpoints. The proof is analytic; random finite test code is not used to quantify all exponents.

value.rationale: This computes the exact worst-base-point symmetric-chord index on a natural two-parameter infinite family of vector-valued sequence spaces. The sharp switch at p=q identifies distinct outer-coordinate and fiber Clarkson mechanisms. The full q>2 law is not a mere substitution into the known q=2 Hilbert case; this is a motivated quantitative phase classification.

limitations: Two-dimensional real fibers with q≥2 only; p is finite and Gamma infinite.
Endpoint q=∞ handled separately, not a limiting numerical test.
